subject: Traffic reallocation advisory — US & EU zones (tenant verification required)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-data.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Traffic reallocation advisory — US & EU zones (tenant verification required)

Hi Samantha / Acme SRE team,

Quick heads up — during the window below we observed an upstream peering disruption affecting egress paths in two of our US zones and a subset of EU POPs. For affected tenants we initiated an automated traffic redirect to alternate regions to preserve latency SLOs.

Time window (observed): 2028-08-28 08:45–09:05 PDT
Impact: Increased 95th percentile token latency and elevated error rates for some EU and US tenants routed through the impacted peering fabric.

Immediate actions we took on your behalf:
- Automatically redirected traffic to our reserve egress for your account (route tag: acme-primary->acme-fallback)
- Enabled prefix-level KV cache warmup to avoid model cold-starts on the failover pool
- Applied an emergency rate cap on non-critical background jobs to protect tail latency

What we need from you (quick verification):
1) Please confirm you see the reroute in your telemetry (hostname prefix: acme.*.redwood-inference.net) and whether any of your requests are still seeing >700ms median token latency.
2) If you rely on region-locked resources (IP allowlists, VPC peering), confirm whether the fallback route needs an IP change or additional ACL entries.

I’ve looped in Marissa (infrastructure) and Ben (customer success) to help with validation and to coordinate any temporary ACL changes or exemptions.

Attachments: reroute-config.json (stub), incident-timeline.csv (stub)

Short timeline and next update in 30 minutes.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-data.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme SRE <sre@acme-data.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 09:28:35 -0400
Subject: Re: Traffic reallocation advisory — US & EU zones (tenant verification required)

Jonas — thanks for the quick note. We are seeing some 5xx spikes in our EU region dashboards around 08:50 UTC but the primary application front-end shows degraded but functional behavior. A few clarifying Qs:

- The hostnames you mentioned — do those require an update to our allowlist? We currently only allow acme.prod.redwood-inference.net in the EU ACL.
- Do you have a short-lived IP range for the fallback?

We can stand by on our side to validate. If you need us to add anything to our firewall, give us the short list and we’ll push it.

— Samantha
Samantha Lee
Platform Ops, Acme Data Systems
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-data.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Traffic reallocation advisory — US & EU zones (tenant verification required)

Samantha — hi, quick technical reply with concrete values so you can validate or open a temporary ACL rule: 

What we routed to: acme-fallback.*.redwood-inference.net (CNAME) -> fallback-pool-eu-us.redwood-inference.net
Temporary IPs (short-lived / changed during post-incident): 34.210.112.0/28, 18.204.33.0/28
TTL: 60s (we’ll keep DNS TTL low while we validate).

Attached is a small reroute-config.json that maps your tenant ID to the fallback pool. The incident-timeline.csv has the event markers we observed (probe failures at 08:46; automated reroute at 08:50; partial restoration attempt at 09:02).

We do not expect persistent request-level token regressions once your allowlist includes the two /28s. If you’d prefer not to change firewall rules, we can add an IP-based proxy entry inside your VPC peering configuration—Ben can help coordinate that.

Next steps on our side:
- 10:30 PDT: run a controlled canary back to primary peering (if upstream fabric shows stability)
- 12:00 PDT: provide a short postmortem draft and a playbook for opt-in rollback to primary routes

Ben — please confirm the proxy option and whether we should provision temporary keys for Acme’s ops team.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: reroute-config.json, incident-timeline.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-data.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 13:01:04 -0700
Subject: Re: Traffic reallocation advisory — US & EU zones (tenant verification required)

Samantha — quick confirm from CS/provisioning side: we can stand up the IP-based proxy in your VPC peering in ~45 minutes and will provide temporary SSH keys + a short HMAC credential set for the health-check endpoint. If you want the firewall change instead that’s fine — we’ll keep the fallback route live until 12:00 PDT and will only switch back after your explicit opt-in or after automated stability validation.

Action items for Acme ops (one-liner):
- Add 34.210.112.0/28 and 18.204.33.0/28 to EU allowlist OR request proxy setup from Ben (reply all with preferred path)
- Reply with any blocked IPs or URLs seen in your WAF logs (if you can attach a snippet, we’ll triage it)

We’ll follow up with a postmortem + remediation checklist by EOD.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-data.com>, Acme SRE <sre@acme-data.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary & follow-up actions — RI-2028-08-28 (Acme)

Hi Samantha / SRE team — thanks again for the quick validation and patience. Below is a concise handoff and the postmortem link.

Brief summary:
- Root cause: transient BGP flap on upstream fabric affecting selective egress prefixes in two US zones and three EU POPs. The flap caused a ~17s probe failure window followed by partial route instability.
- Customer impact: increased tail latency and intermittent 5xx for a subset of requests from EU-origin traffic. No data loss or model-state corruption observed.
- Mitigation: automatic traffic redirection to the fallback pool (as communicated). We kept DNS TTL at 60s and opened proxy option for customers unwilling/unable to change ACLs.

What we are delivering now: 
- Postmortem draft (PDF) and incident timeline uploaded: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cPostmortemLink
- Incident record: https://status.redwood-inference.com/incidents/RI-2028-08-28
- Internal ticket for follow-up (benchmarks & kernel selection review): JIRA SUP-1234

Requested customer actions:
- Confirm when your allowlist is updated or if you want us to provision the proxy (reply: proxy || allowlist)
- If you saw any client-side failures after 09:30 PDT, please attach a snippet of the request/response and timestamp so we can correlate logs

Planned next steps (internal + customer-facing):
- EOD: share final postmortem and any recommended ingress/egress hardening for customers in EU
- Next week: schedule a short review call if you’d like a walkthrough of the timeline and the recommended config changes (I can set aside Wed 10–11 PDT).

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf

Thanks,
Jonas
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
